record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
record.context_brief: Volume from random samples of a polytope
record.original_question: Can the volume of a polytope with a bounded number of facets be computed efficiently from a random sample drawn from the polytope, without using an annealing sequence of changing sampling distributions?

evidence.quote: On the other hand, it remains open to efficiently compute the volume from a random sample for polytopes with a bounded number of facets.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded full-dimensional polytope given by a system of linear inequalities with at most $m$ facets, where $m = \mathrm{poly}(n)$ (or more generally, $m$ is bounded by a fixed polynomial in the dimension $n$). Suppose one is given access to a random sample of points drawn (independently) from the uniform distribution on $P$.

Design an algorithm that, given only such a single-distribution random sample from $P$ (i.e., without making use of an annealing schedule of intermediate sampling distributions that interpolate between an easy distribution and the uniform distribution on $P$), computes a $(1\pm\varepsilon)$-approximation of the volume $\mathrm{vol}(P)$ in time polynomial in $n$, $m$, and $1/\varepsilon$, with high probability.

The question is whether such an efficient single-distribution sample-based volume estimation algorithm exists for polytopes with a bounded (polynomial) number of facets, or to prove that no such algorithm exists.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a definitive resolution. Modern volume-approximation algorithms and software (e.g., volesti and related random-walk methods such as Hit-and-Run, Cooling Gaussians, Cooling Bodies, Sequence of Balls) continue to rely on annealing-style sequences of distributions, and no result was found that achieves efficient volume computation from a single sampling distribution for polytopes with a bounded number of facets. The status appears to remain unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: volesti: Volume Approximation and Sampling for Convex Polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Implements Sequence of Balls, Cooling Gaussians, and Cooling convex Bodies — all annealing-based volume algorithms.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art polytope volume algorithms still use annealing sequences of distributions.

status_evidence.title: Efficient Random-Walk Methods for Approximating Polytope Volume
status_evidence.snippet: Random-walk methods for polytope volume approximation rely on multi-phase sampling.
status_evidence.claim: No single-distribution sample-based volume algorithm for bounded-facet polytopes is reported.
